# Qarinah

> One automatic coding context harness for every Git worktree.

Qarinah gives every Git worktree an isolated, cited project ledger, automatically records compact completed-turn checkpoints, and links related checkouts into one repository context graph. Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Kimi, Antigravity, Freebuff, and compatible tools can continue from verified context without mixing parallel branches or replaying the complete project history.

This file is a convenience map for tools that choose to read it. It is not a ranking signal or a substitute for the canonical documentation.

## Direct facts

- Qarinah is a worktree-aware context system for software projects and an independent local tool; Maqam is an optional approval integration.
- Each initialized Git worktree receives its own workspace ID, worktree ID, ledger, derived SQLite state, graph, and cited context packs. Related worktrees share a repository ID and can be inspected together without merging their records.
- Qarinah is a local, evidence-linked project-memory compiler for coding agents. It is not a complete autonomous-agent runtime or a general personalization service.
- The alternatives guide is a representative category comparison, not a performance ranking or a claim that Qarinah is universally better than adjacent products.
- Qarinah, Maqam, Cockroach Browser, and Cockroach Crawler are separate projects by Ajnas N B. The ecosystem guide distinguishes them from third-party tools maintained by their own projects.
- Cockroach Browser uses Playwright. Cockroach Crawler discloses Trafilatura as the optional quality dependency. The ecosystem guide does not claim that those established projects were created by Qarinah's author.
- Qarinah's primary workflow is verified handoffs between coding agents.
- Qarinah 0.4.0 passed 16 / 16 deterministic continuity scenarios across three actual Git worktrees, including separate workspace identities, retrieval, conflicts, session receipts, and four compaction states.
- The VS Code/Cursor panel shows the same local searchable graph, decisions/tools/outcomes/conflicts timeline, exact session receipts, and sibling-worktree comparison as the CLI/dashboard projection.
- Host installation is previewable and reversible for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Kimi, Antigravity, and Freebuff; support describes project configuration and does not claim identical native capture in every host.
- Qarinah's optional automatic harness records a deterministic compact checkpoint after a supported completed turn; optional host-model compaction receives only the already bounded pack and is not enabled by the automatic hook.
- Qarinah initializes a rebuildable SQLite WAL/FTS5 read model, graph, index, and Markdown view when a workspace is initialized.
- Complete setup records a bounded project-structure graph, and `qarinah overview` explains memory counts, latest outcomes, languages, directories, and relationships.
- `qarinah import` streams supported visible Codex, Claude, and portable JSONL archives. Compact mode stores one cited summary per session; full mode stores supported visible events in a content-authorized workspace.
- Qarinah excludes hidden and encrypted reasoning record types from archive import and cannot recover content that was never captured or imported.
- Qarinah supports reviewed Codex and Claude Code integrations that can use the same explicitly opted-in project record.
- The published evaluator measured 98.71% less estimated repeated input context in its compared task set: 442,113 estimated input-context tokens became 5,682 while every required target was directly covered in the top five.
- That compared slice contained 436,431 fewer estimated input-context tokens, and the evaluated full-history baseline contained 77.81 times as many estimated tokens as the compiled Qarinah pack: a 77.81:1 baseline-to-pack ratio.
- At a flat $3 per million uncached input tokens, the aggregate six-fixture slice estimates $1.326339 for full-history replay versus $0.017046 for Qarinah, saving $1.309293 per repeat. This is a transparent arithmetic equivalent, not a provider invoice.
- A separate deterministic scale regression ranked the correct target first for 380 / 380 file-specific exact and typo-tolerant queries across 40-, 50-, and 100-file projects.
- The 98.71% and 77.81:1 results are not universal provider-billing, session-length, latency, or answer-quality guarantees. Qarinah improves provenance and inspectability but cannot guarantee a model answer is correct.
- Qarinah requires no hosted memory account, embedding API, vector database, or Qarinah API key for local operation.
- Qarinah is open source under Apache License 2.0.

## Technical documentation

- [Features](https://qarinah.io/docs/features/): Shipped project-memory, context-compilation, integration, team, export, and verification capabilities.
- [Worktree context](https://qarinah.io/docs/worktree-context/): Repository and worktree identities, isolated ledgers, grouped graph inspection, hashes, and operating boundaries.
- [Project overview](https://qarinah.io/docs/project-overview/): Beginner-readable project memory and codebase summary.
- [Agent archive import](https://qarinah.io/docs/agent-archive-import/): Large JSONL import modes, limits, portable format, exclusions, and verification.
- [Private projects](https://qarinah.io/docs/private-projects/): Data-handling controls and legal boundary for NDA-conscious use.
- [CLI reference](https://qarinah.io/docs/cli/): Every command, option, stdin mode, exit code, and machine-readable output.
- [JavaScript API reference](https://qarinah.io/docs/api/): Public exports, types, functions, and bounded programmatic workflows.
- [Host integrations](https://qarinah.io/docs/integrations/): Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, CLI, and consent-gated MCP integration guidance.
- [MCP guide](https://qarinah.io/docs/mcp/): Configure diagnostic-only or explicitly authorized, zero-write context retrieval.
- [Local memory dashboard](https://qarinah.io/docs/dashboard/): Inspect responsive snapshots or live loopback views of real retained activity across explicitly selected, separately identified local projects.
- [Azure evaluation](https://qarinah.io/docs/azure-evaluation/): Decide when local SQLite is enough and when an explicit Azure AI Search and Blob Storage evaluation may be appropriate.
- [Team memory](https://qarinah.io/docs/team-memory/): Setup, dashboards, freshness, multi-repository packs, encrypted sync, evaluation, and causal receipts.
- [Token-efficient context](https://qarinah.io/docs/token-efficient-context/): How Qarinah selects compact evidence without making the complete transcript the prompt.
- [Task recipes](https://qarinah.io/docs/recipes/): Copyable workflows for refactors, debugging, migrations, research, releases, and handoffs.
- [Architecture](https://qarinah.io/docs/architecture/): Append-only event record, deterministic derived state, typed graph, retrieval, and context-pack compilation.
- [Benchmarks](https://qarinah.io/docs/benchmarks/): Reproducible methodology, qualifications, commands, and committed results.
- [Security model](https://qarinah.io/docs/security/): Workspace trust, capture consent, redaction, integrity, disclosure boundaries, and known limits.
- [Interoperability](https://qarinah.io/docs/interoperability/): Deterministic Markdown, JSON, graph, and Google Open Knowledge Format exports.
- [Troubleshooting](https://qarinah.io/docs/troubleshooting/): Diagnose trust, capture, rebuild, query, MCP, and host-integration failures.
- [FAQ](https://qarinah.io/docs/faq/): Direct answers about storage, privacy, context reduction, hosts, and operating boundaries.
- [Migration guide](https://qarinah.io/docs/migrations/): Upgrade persisted Qarinah workspaces safely.
- [Technical white paper](https://qarinah.io/paper/): Implementation-backed paper version 1.5 for Qarinah 0.4.0. Version 1.5 has no version DOI until separately deposited; the persistent paper-series DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.21547684 and published v1.4 remains historical.
